claim: The press needs 81.2 kN on the 290 x 140 mm block face for 2 MPa
law: F = p A

claim: Compacting a 5 % cement mix to 2 MPa gives blocks that can meet the R3 strength class with suitable soil
law: Auroville Earth Institute: CSEB pressed at 2 to 4 MPa with about 5 % cement; the Auram press 3000 works at 2.7 to 5.3 MPa
check: 2 MPa is the low end of practice; strength depends on soil, mix and curing and is measured in block tests (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: The lever and toggle give a force ratio of 173:1 at the crank stop
law: Toggle 1 / (2 tan 6 deg) times grip radius over the connecting link's arm (virtual work)

claim: Two people on the 1.71 m grip path supply the compaction work of the softer design soil
law: Conservation of energy or mass

claim: Each of two operators pulls no more than 500 N at the peak, with the softer design soil
law: Peak grip force from the force ratio and the soil law (CAL section 4b); project limit 500 N per operator (R5, PR-005); ISO 11228-2 screening to assess
check: 405 N against 500 N, but it rests on the assumed soil law (S6) and on equal shares between the two operators; measure on partner soils

claim: Soil pressure in the mold rises tenfold over the last 14 mm of the stroke (10 to 20 mm)
law: Assumed exponential compaction law; no measured curve for the partner's soils
check: Measure pressure against travel on partner soils (compaction test); S4, S5 and the fill window rest on it

claim: Every load-path member stays below yield at the 173 kN design load (1,000 N at the grip at the stop)
law: Bending, shear, bearing, net section and buckling against yield of S235/S250 plate, A53 pipe and 42CrMo4 +QT pins (CAL Table 5)

claim: A 10 kg scale with 50 g divisions can hold the fill to its window of 0 to +206 g
law: Scale division against half the fill window (CAL section 5)
check: 50 g division against a half-width of 103 g for the base soil, but the softer design soil has a window of about 0 to +153 g (half-width 76 g), a division is not the scale's accuracy (a low-cost 10 kg scale is about 50 to 100 g) and a 1 % moisture swing moves the dry mass by about 70 g: confirm scale accuracy and moisture control

claim: The 40 mm 42CrMo4 +QT toggle pins stay below yield in bending at the 173 kN design load
law: Pin in a clevis: link force per side times the distance between bearing centres (base pin 36 mm arm), M / (pi d^3 / 32) against Rp0.2 750 MPa for 16 < d <= 40 mm; the 35 mm C45 pins of CAL v0.6 failed (388 MPa against 370 MPa at the nominal load, 826 MPa at 173 kN)

claim: The base pin lugs carry the design load within the bush bearing allowable
law: Bearing p = F / (2 t d) on 2 x 28 mm lugs at 40 mm, allowable 100 MPa for hardened greased bushes (assumed); the 20 mm lugs on 35 mm reached 124 MPa

claim: Welded members last 50,000 blocks in fatigue
law: Nominal stress range per block against a FAT 71 detail at 50,000 cycles (EN 1993-1-9 method)

claim: The turned toggle pins last 50,000 blocks in bending fatigue
law: Pulsating range against 0.5 Rm x 0.7 for surface and size (Rm 1,000 MPa minimum, 42CrMo4 +QT; first-order)

claim: Released at the stop, the lever kicks back with about 47 J
law: Strain energy 0.5 F d with 1.0 mm soil rebound (assumed) and the column stretch

claim: One person ejects the block with 470 N or less on the eject lever
law: Wall friction 0.1 MPa residual lateral pressure x 0.6 x wall area, plus piston and block weight, over the 10.3:1 eject ratio (assumed residual pressure)
check: 469 N against 500 N, a margin of about 6 % that rests on the assumed 0.1 MPa residual pressure (at 0.2 MPa the force would be about 930 N): measure on partner soils

claim: A crew of four makes about 296 blocks in an 8 h day
law: Makiga manual press, 290 x 140 mm blocks, about 500 a day with a crew of four (Engineering for Change); EarthPress cycle 85 s assumed (CAL section 9)

claim: Curing blocks bind about 0.23 kg of water per kg of cement
law: Non-evaporable water of fully hydrated Portland cement about 0.23 g/g (Powers and Brownyard; Neville, Properties of Concrete)
check: Used only for the cured mass in the flow figure; 712 kg per 100 blocks

claim: CSEB walling embodies 25 % or less of the CO2 of fired brick of equal volume
law: Auroville Earth Institute factors: 49 kg CO2/m3 for 5 % CSEB, 643 kg CO2/m3 for locally fired brick

claim: Lime at about 8 % stabilizes clay-rich soils, with a longer curing period than cement
law: Lime and clay react slowly (cation exchange, then pozzolanic calcium silicate and aluminate hydrates); needs enough clay and moisture
check: Starting value only; wet-strength tests on partner soils decide the dose and the curing time (TRL 4, on hold)

claim: Sieving dry soil raises respirable crystalline silica, so damp sieving and an FFP2 or N95 respirator are specified
law: Crystalline silica is carcinogenic to humans (IARC Group 1, Monograph 100C); OSHA PEL 50 ug/m3 over 8 h (29 CFR 1926.1153)
check: Hazard and controls stated in PRC, BLD and RSK; no exposure claim is made

claim: Wet cement can burn skin and eyes, so gloves and eye protection are specified
law: Portland cement safety data sheets: causes skin irritation and serious eye damage (hazard statements H315, H318); wet mix is strongly alkaline
check: Hazard and controls stated in PRC, BLD and RSK

claim: Two people can lift the heaviest piece of the press
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg per person for occasional lifts; two people share the piece
check: 22.2 kg per person if the load halves exactly, but team lifting usually reduces each person's share of the capacity and the 25 kg figure is for ideal conditions: to assess; lift with a trolley, a hoist or four people

claim: The grip stays at 0.8 m or higher through the stroke, with the peak force at 1.0 m or higher
law: Lever kinematics (CAL section 3); R5 band

claim: The mold walls bulge far less than the 2 mm block tolerance at 2 MPa
law: Fixed-fixed wall strip with the belt, lateral pressure 0.5 x vertical (assumed K0)

claim: Option B: two people on a 1.2 m capstan turn the screw at the 81 kN pressing force within 500 N each
law: Power screw torque T = F d2 / 2 tan(lambda + phi'), lambda 7.0 deg, phi' 8.8 deg (mu 0.15), T 430 N m; grips 0.53 m from the axis

claim: Option B: the two-start screw is self-locking, so it holds the load without a pawl
law: Self-locking when the lead angle is below the friction angle
check: lambda 7.0 deg against phi' 8.8 deg at mu 0.15 but 5.9 deg at mu 0.10 (well greased): not self-locking when greased; a brake or a single-start screw would be needed

claim: Option B: a 90 mm bronze nut carries the pressing force within its bearing allowable
law: Thread bearing p = F / (pi d2 H1 n); hand press, steel screw on bronze nut, 17 to 24 MPa (Shigley, Table 8-4)

claim: Option B: the screw's root section stays below yield at the largest force two people can make
law: Root diameter 32 mm; two people at 500 N on 0.53 m give the largest force; C45 yield 340 MPa (first-order)

claim: Option B: a crew of four makes about 225 blocks a day
law: Makiga manual press about 500 a day (Engineering for Change); option B cycle 111 s with 14 unloaded turns each way (227 a day)

claim: Option B: the operators supply the pressing work through a screw of about 43 % efficiency
law: Conservation of energy or mass

claim: Option C: about 25 blows of a 20 kg weight falling 450 mm give standard Proctor compaction energy
law: ASTM D698 standard effort 592.7 kJ/m3 over the 3.65 L block; blow energy m g h

claim: Option C: impact compaction at standard Proctor effort reaches the density of 2 MPa static pressing
law: Impact and static compaction give different density profiles; impact from the top densifies the top layer most
check: No source equates the two for CSEB; test blocks needed

claim: Option C: each of two people pulls under 500 N on the rope, even when lifting the plunger for filling
law: Weight, rod and plunger about 40 kg, shared by two over the head pulley

claim: Option C: the operators' sustained power stays within human capacity
law: 25 blows of 88 J in 100 s, shared by two; sustained adult output about 75 W

claim: Option C: a crew of four makes about 160 blocks a day
law: Makiga manual press about 500 a day (Engineering for Change); option C cycle 160 s (25 blows at 15 a minute plus 60 s)

claim: Option C: the mold, plunger and floor stop survive the impact peak force
law: Impact force depends on the soil's stiffness at the end of compaction, not yet known
check: To be estimated from a measured soil stiffness (S6)
